q1.question:
As discussed in class, working with low-level functions and system calls can be tricky because unlike most normal functions, they can fail. For each of the following scenarios involving timeit, identify which low-level function or system call (used in timeit) would fail:

  1. User has passes a program that does not exist. ____
  2. User has reached their limit of processes. ____

q2.question:
In timeit, you implemented both the context manager protocol and the iterator protocol in the Timer class

: 
with Timer(['sleep', '1']) as timer:
    for elapsed in timer:
        print(elapsed)

Which of the following statements regarding are true (choose all that apply)?

responses.context_process: The context manager protocol was used to manage the creation and cleanup of the child process.
responses.iterator_process: The iterator protocol was used to manage the creation and cleanup of the child process.
responses.context_elapsed: The context manager protocol was used to track the elapsed time.
responses.iterator_elapsed: The iterator protocol was used to track the elapsed time.

q3.question: An eager student proposes changing timeit such that the child process sets an signal.alarm before calling os.execvp so that it can os.kill itself if the signal handler is invoked. Would this work?

responses.nope_1: Nope, only a parent process can set an signal.alarm.
responses.nope_3: Nope, os.execvp loads new code so the signal.alarm handler is removed.

q4.question: A malicious student proposes changing timeit such that the child process changes the Timer.pid attribute before calling os.execvp in order to prevent the parent from killing the child process. Would this work?

responses.nope_1: Nope, only a parent process can change object attributes.
responses.nope_2: Nope, a process cannot modify object attributes.
responses.nope_3: Nope, the parent and child have separate address spaces.

q5.question: A concerned student proposes changing timeit such that the parent process sends SIGSTOP to the child process when signal.alarm handler is invoked. Would this work?

responses.nope_1: Nope, because the child process can ignore SIGSTOP.
responses.nope_2: Nope, because only the kernel can use this signal.
responses.nope_3: Nope, because this only suspends the process and does not terminate it.
